text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.67% today as oil prices stabilized after several days of weakness. The stock had fallen sharply over the past two weeks amid hopes for a near-term end to the Iran conflict — Trump's comments suggesting the war would "end fairly soon" spooked energy investors on November 10th, sending Brent crude briefly below $90 a barrel. Today's bounce reflects a modest recovery in crude prices (US oil at $99.64, still down from earlier levels) and some reassessment that a quick resolution remains uncertain despite the administration's optimistic rhetoric.

The backdrop remains genuinely mixed for oil companies. While the Iran de-escalation talk has depressed crude prices, recent midterm election results pushing back against the GOP and favoring renewable energy add longer-term headwinds for traditional energy. ConocoPhillips still sits down 7.5% over two weeks — the market is pricing in structural weakness even if near-term geopolitical anxiety eases.
